Prealgebra · Lesson 4.2

Equivalent Fractions

Solve this lesson →All lessons

One ranger cuts a trail into 44 equal stretches and marks 3443​ of the way out. Another cuts the same trail into 1212 stretches and marks 912129​. They walk out and find their ribbons on the same patch of dirt. Two different fractions can name the same amount, and there is a rule for when they do.

Problem
Trail cut into 44 stretches, then into 1212. Every third stake of the second ranger lands on a stake of the first. Which stake sits on 3443​? Write as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Her ribbon at 3443​ is the third of her four marks, so three full stretches of hers lie behind it. Each one of those stretches is worth how many of his little pieces?
  • Three of her stretches sit before the ribbon, and each one is worth 33 of his pieces, so 3×3=93×3=9 of his pieces bring you exactly to the ribbon. His ninth stake is at 912129​.
Show the full solution
Her ribbon sits after 33 of her 44 stretches, and each of her stretches holds 33 of his pieces, so 3×3=93×3=9 of his pieces reach the ribbon. His ninth stake, 9/129/12​, stands on the same patch of dirt. That is the same as 34×3343​×33​. Multiplying top and bottom by the same number renames the point without moving it.
Problem
A fudge tray has 33 strips, and 22 go to an order (2332​). Each strip is re-scored into 55 mini strips. Write the new fraction name for the order as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • The fudge in the order did not change at all, only how it is sliced. Count two things in the new mini strips, how many mini strips make up the whole tray, and how many make up the order.
  • Each of the 3 strips becomes 5 mini strips, so the tray holds 3×53×5 of them. Each of the 2 order strips also becomes 5 mini strips, so the order is 2×52×5. Put the order count over the tray count.
Show the full solution
The tray had 33 strips and each becomes 55 mini strips, so the tray holds 3×5=153×5=15. The order was 22 strips, which becomes 2×5=102×5=10. So the order is 10/1510/15​. Slicing every piece into kk smaller pieces multiplies the top and the bottom by the same kk, which is why the amount of fudge never changes.
Problem
A coach multiplies top and bottom of 5665​ by 44. The extra 44 appears on both floors and cancels, leaving the same value. Write the bigger name as abba​.
Show a hint
  • You are not changing the value, you are just renaming it with larger numbers. Multiply the top by 44 to get the new top, and multiply the bottom by 44 to get the new bottom. The factor of 44 on top and the factor of 44 on the bottom cancel in the single division, which is why the split stays the same.
  • Top is 5×45×4. Bottom is 6×46×4. Compute each one and stack the new top over the new bottom as abba​.
Show the full solution
Multiply the top by 44 and the bottom by 44. The top becomes 5×4=205×4=20 and the bottom becomes 6×4=246×4=24, so the bigger name is 20/2420/24​. A fraction is one division, so a factor of 44 on top and a matching 44 on the bottom cancel, leaving 55 divided by 66 again.
Key idea
Equivalent fractions. For any nonzero kk, ab=a×kb×k.ba​=b×ka×k​. A fraction is one number, aa divided by bb. A kk on the top and a matching kk on the bottom cancel, so the value does not change. The picture agrees. Cut each of your bb pieces into kk smaller pieces and you have kk times as many, each kk times thinner, so the total is the same. Multiplying the top and bottom to get bigger numbers is called building the fraction up.
Problem
A counter must display fractions over 2121. A runner is 2332​ done. Find kk where 3k=213k=21, scale the top. How many of 2121 lights should show?
Show a hint
  • The bottom of the fraction has to go from 3 to 21 without changing the actual amount. The only honest way to do that is to multiply the bottom by some whole number kk. Ask yourself what you multiply 3 by to land exactly on 21, since that same kk is how many small pieces each third gets cut into.
  • You need 3×k=213×k=21, so k=21÷3=7k=21÷3=7. Cutting each third into 7 means you must also multiply the top by 7. Compute 2×72×7.
Show the full solution
You need 3×k=213×k=21, so k=21÷3=7k=21÷3=7. Multiply the top by that same 77, giving 2×7=142×7=14, so 23=2×73×7=1421.32​=3×72×7​=2114​. The counter should light 1414​ of its 2121 lights. Aim at the bottom first, then copy that same multiplier onto the top, or the value shifts.
Problem
Scoreboard shows 18242418​. Divide by 22 to get 912129​, then divide by 33. Stop when top and bottom share no factor above 11. Write the result as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • You already did the first cut, going from 18242418​ to 912129​. The seed tells you the next shared factor is 3. Apply that one division to both the top and the bottom and see where you stop.
  • Take 912129​ and divide both numbers by 3. The top becomes 9÷39÷3 and the bottom becomes 12÷312÷3. Work out those two numbers and write the fraction they form.
Show the full solution
From 912129​, divide both numbers by 33. That gives 9÷312÷3=3412÷39÷3​=43​, and 33 and 44 share no factor above 11, so this is where you stop. The smallest name is 3/43/4​. Reducing is building up run backward, dividing out a shared factor instead of multiplying one in.
Key idea
Building up and reducing. Multiply the top and bottom by the same nonzero kk to build up, ab=a×kb×kba​=b×ka×k​. That gives a bigger name with more, smaller pieces. The same rule in reverse is called reducing. When some dd divides both top and bottom evenly, divide both by dd, ab=a÷db÷dba​=b÷da÷d​. That gives a smaller name with fewer, larger pieces. Either direction only adds or removes a shared factor inside one division, so the value is the same.
Problem
A coach writes a split as 8412012084​. Find gcd⁡(84,120)gcd(84,120), divide both top and bottom by it in one stroke, and write 8412012084​ in lowest terms as abba​.
Show a hint
  • The idea is that you do not have to peel factors one by one. One number can strip them all at once. What is the largest number that divides both 84 and 120 cleanly? Break each into its prime factors and grab everything they share.
  • Both numbers are even, both are divisible by 4, and both are divisible by 3, so 4×34×3 divides each. That makes gcd⁡(84,120)=12gcd(84,120)=12. Now compute 84÷1284÷12 for the new top and 120÷12120÷12 for the new bottom.
Show the full solution
Factor both numbers. 84=2×2×3×784=2×2×3×7 and 120=2×2×2×3×5120=2×2×2×3×5, so they share two 22s and a 33, making gcd⁡(84,120)=12gcd(84,120)=12. Then 84÷12=784÷12=7 and 120÷12=10120÷12=10, so lowest terms is 7/107/10​. One pass is enough because the gcd already holds every prime the two numbers share.
Problem
Shared primes of 126126 and 350350 are 22 and 77. Multiply them for the common factor, divide both by it. Write 126350350126​ in lowest terms as a/ba/b.
Show a hint
  • Lay the two prime lists side by side. A prime can only cancel if it appears in both lists. Which primes show up in the top list and the bottom list?
  • The shared primes are 22 and 77, so the common factor is 2×7=142×7=14. Divide both 126126 and 350350 by 1414.
Show the full solution
The top is 126=2×3×3×7126=2×3×3×7 and the bottom is 350=2×5×5×7350=2×5×5×7. Only the 22 and the 77 appear in both lists, so the common factor is 2×7=142×7=14. Dividing gives 126÷14=9126÷14=9 and 350÷14=25350÷14=25, so the gears in lowest terms are 9/259/25​. A prime cancels only when it sits on both floors, which is why the 33s and 55s stay put.
Key idea
Lowest terms. A fraction is in lowest terms when its top and bottom share no factor bigger than 11. In symbols, gcd⁡(top,bottom)=1gcd(top,bottom)=1. If the gcd is larger, a shared factor is still there, so find gcd⁡(top,bottom)gcd(top,bottom) and divide the top and bottom by it. That one division removes every shared factor at once. A single number has infinitely many fraction names, and exactly one of them is in lowest terms. So two fractions are the same number exactly when they reduce to the same lowest-terms form.
Problem
An app stores 2552​, but the display only allows bottom ≤40≤40. Allowed bottoms are 5k≤405k≤40. How many different names fit?
Show a hint
  • Forget the top number for a moment. The only thing that decides whether a name fits is its bottom, and the bottom is always 5k5k. So you are really asking how many whole numbers kk keep 5k5k from going past 4040. That is just counting multiples of 55, the kind of thing you did back in Chapter 3.
  • List the bottoms in order. With k=1k=1 the bottom is 55, with k=2k=2 it is 1010, and so on. Keep going as long as the bottom stays at or below 4040, then count how many you wrote down.
Show the full solution
Every allowed name is 2k5k5k2k​, so the only rule is 5k≤405k≤40. Dividing, 40÷5=840÷5=8, so kk runs 11 through 88, since k=9k=9 would push the bottom to 4545. That is 88​ names. The whole family of names for a fraction is just the multiples of its bottom, so counting names is counting multiples.

To compare two fractions, give them the same denominator first. Then both count pieces of one size, so the fraction with the bigger top is larger. Adding fractions uses this same shared-denominator step.

Problem
Slopes 5665​ and 7887​ over shared bottom 2424: sixths ×4×4, eighths ×3×3. Compare tops. Write the steeper slope as abba​.
Show a hint
  • You cannot compare the tops while the bottoms disagree. Force both fractions onto the same bottom of 2424 first, then the bigger top wins. Multiplying top and bottom by the same number does not change a fraction's value, it just renames it.
  • Multiply 5665​ by 4444​ to get 20242420​, and multiply 7887​ by 3333​ to get 21242421​. Now both bottoms are 2424, so compare the tops 2020 and 2121. The bigger top names the steeper ramp, and your answer should be its original unbuilt fraction.
Show the full solution
Put both slopes over 2424. 56=5×46×4=2024,78=7×38×3=212465​=6×45×4​=2420​,87​=8×37×3​=2421​ Since 21>2021>20, the west ramp is steeper, with slope 7/87/8​. Tops are only comparable once the bottoms match, because only then are you counting pieces of the same size.
Problem
Is 46=6964​=96​? Compute 4×94×9 and 6×66×6. Equal products mean equal fractions. Enter the common product if equal, else 00.
Show a hint
  • Multiplying 4664​ by 6×96×9 cancels the bottom 66 and leaves 4×94×9. Multiplying 6996​ by the same 6×96×9 cancels the bottom 99 and leaves 6×66×6. Now you only have to compare two whole-number products, no fractions left.
  • Work out 4×94×9 and 6×66×6 separately. If they land on the same number, that number is your answer. If they differ, the answer is 00.
Show the full solution
4×9=364×9=36 and 6×6=366×6=36. The two products agree, so 4664​ and 6996​ are the same number and the common product is 3636​. Multiplying both fractions by 6×96×9 clears the bottoms and leaves exactly those crossed products, so ab=cdba​=dc​ exactly when a×d=b×ca×d=b×c.
Key idea
Cross-multiplication test. The fractions abba​ and cddc​ are the same number exactly when ad=bcad=bc, so neither one needs reducing. Multiply the top of each by the bottom of the other and compare. To see why, re-cut both to the shared bottom b×db×d. The first becomes a×da×d of those small pieces and the second c×bc×b. The pieces are the same size, so the fractions are equal exactly when the counts match. If the products differ, the bigger product goes with the bigger fraction, so the test also tells you which fraction is larger.
Fun fact
Reducing shrinks the numbers written, not the amount. The gcd from Chapter 3 does the whole job in one step.
Problem
Master fraction 814148​. Three locks: 12212112​, 20353520​, 16303016​. Cross-product test each. How many equal 814148​?
Show a hint
  • You do not need to simplify a single fraction here. For each stamped lock cddc​, build the two products 8×d8×d and 14×c14×c and just ask whether they land on the same number. Equal products mean the lock belongs, different products mean it does not.
  • Take them one at a time. For 12212112​, compare 8×218×21 with 14×1214×12. For 20353520​, compare 8×358×35 with 14×2014×20. For 16303016​, compare 8×308×30 with 14×1614×16. Count up how many of the three pairs come out matching.
Show the full solution
Each lock cddc​ matches when 8×d=14×c8×d=14×c. For 12212112​, 8×21=1688×21=168 and 14×12=16814×12=168, a match. For 20353520​, 8×35=2808×35=280 and 14×20=28014×20=280, a match. For 16303016​, 8×30=2408×30=240 but 14×16=22414×16=224, so that one fails. 22​ locks equal 814148​. The near miss gets caught without reducing anything.
Problem
Ticks n3636n​ for n=1…36n=1…36. Gold plate only where gcd⁡(n,36)=1gcd(n,36)=1. Since 36=22×3236=22×32, nn must miss multiples of 22 and 33. How many ticks are gold plated?
Show a hint
  • You are really counting how many numbers from 1 to 36 are coprime to 36, meaning they have no factor of 2 and no factor of 3. It is faster to count the ones that get thrown away than to check all 36 by hand. How many multiples of 2 are in 1 to 36, and how many multiples of 3?
  • There are 18 multiples of 2 and 12 multiples of 3 in the range, but the multiples of 6 got counted in both groups, so subtract them back once. That removes 18+12−6=2418+12−6=24 numbers. Whatever is left out of 36 is your answer.
Show the full solution
Count the tops that fail and subtract. From 11 to 3636 there are 36÷2=1836÷2=18 multiples of 22 and 36÷3=1236÷3=12 multiples of 33, and the 36÷6=636÷6=6 multiples of 66 got counted in both groups, so 18+12−6=2418+12−6=24 tops fail. That leaves 36−24=1236−24=12​ gold ticks. Counting failures beats testing all 3636, as long as you subtract the multiples of 66 once to fix the double count.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A window box is split into 33 equal sections, and flowers fill the first section (1331​). Re-scoring into 1212 cells: how many cells do the flowers cover?
Show the solution
The 33 sections become 3×4=123×4=12 cells, so the bottom grew by a factor of 44 and the top has to grow by 44 as well. 13=1×43×4=41231​=3×41×4​=124​ The flowers cover 44​ cells. Re-scoring does not move the flowers, it just counts the same patch in smaller pieces.
Practice
Five sections report harmony fractions: 812128​, 610106​, 10151510​, 14212114​, 912129​. How many equal 2332​?
Show the solution
Cross multiply against 2332​, so abba​ matches when 3a=2b3a=2b. For 812128​, 24=2424=24, a match. For 610106​, 1818 against 2020, no. For 10151510​, 30=3030=30, a match. For 14212114​, 42=4242=42, a match. For 912129​, 2727 against 2424, no. Three of the five pass, so 33​.
Practice
A hose covers 2772​ of a garden row (22 of 77 beds). Every bed is re-cut into 44 patches. After the re-cut, how many equal patches make up the whole row?
Show the solution
Each of the 77 beds splits into 44 patches, so the row now holds 7×4=287×4=28​ equal patches. The watered share becomes 2×4=82×4=8 of them, and 828288​ reduces back to 2772​, so the coverage never changed, only the piece size.
Practice
A jar is 10252510​ full. Reduce to lowest terms by dividing by the common divisor. Write the simplest name as a/ba/b.
Show the solution
Both 1010 and 2525 are multiples of 55, and 55 is the largest number dividing both. Dividing gives 10÷5=210÷5=2 on top and 25÷5=525÷5=5 on the bottom, so the simplest name is 2/52/5​. Since 22 and 55 share no factor above 11, it cannot shrink any further.
Practice
3030 yes votes out of 4242 total. Find gcd⁡(30,42)gcd(30,42), divide top and bottom by it. Write 30424230​ in lowest terms as abba​.
Show the solution
30=6×530=6×5 and 42=6×742=6×7, and nothing larger divides both, so gcd⁡(30,42)=6gcd(30,42)=6. Divide the top and bottom by that 66 in one step. 3042=30÷642÷6=574230​=42÷630÷6​=75​ Lowest terms is 5/75/7​, since 55 and 77 share no factor bigger than 11.
Practice
A label reads 15282815​. Before reducing, check: is it already in lowest terms? A fraction is simplest when gcd⁡(top,bottom)=1gcd(top,bottom)=1. Find gcd⁡(15,28)gcd(15,28).
Show the solution
15=3×515=3×5 and 28=2×2×728=2×2×7. The two lists share no prime at all, so the only whole number dividing both is 11​. A gcd of 11 is exactly what lowest terms means, so 15282815​ has nothing left to cancel.
Practice
A reading of 712127​ must be rewritten over 4848. Find kk where 12×k=4812×k=48, then scale the top by kk. What top number is stored over 4848?
Show the solution
The bottom grows from 1212 to 4848, so k=48÷12=4k=48÷12=4. Multiply the top by that same 44, giving 7×4=287×4=28​, so 712=2848127​=4828​. Scaling only one floor would change the value, which is why the same kk has to go on both.
Practice
A battery shows 56646456​ charged. Divide top and bottom by their gcd. What is 56646456​ in lowest terms as a/ba/b?
Show the solution
56=8×756=8×7 and 64=8×864=8×8, so gcd⁡(56,64)=8gcd(56,64)=8. Dividing both parts by 88 gives 5664=56÷864÷8=78.6456​=64÷856÷8​=87​. The battery is 7/87/8​ charged. Since 77 is prime and does not divide 88, nothing is left to cancel.
Practice
Sensor 1: 814148​. Sensor 2: 12212112​. Cross-multiply: compare 8×218×21 against 14×1214×12. Do they name the same point? Enter yes or no.
Show the solution
8×21=1688×21=168 and 14×12=16814×12=168. The two diagonals match, so the readings name the same point, yesyes​. Reducing agrees, since 814148​ and 12212112​ both come down to 4774​.
Practice
A dial stores 5885​ as x4040x​. Cross-multiplying gives 5×40=8×x5×40=8×x. What is xx?
Show the solution
Cross-multiplying x40=5840x​=85​ gives 8×x=5×40=2008×x=5×40=200, so x=200÷8=25x=200÷8=25​. Checking, 25404025​ reduces by 55 back to 5885​.
Practice
A scanner counted 162162 clean jars out of 252252 total. Reduce 162252252162​ all the way to simplest form abba​.
Show the solution
Factor both numbers. 162=2×34162=2×34 and 252=22×32×7252=22×32×7, so the shared part is one 22 and two 33s, which makes gcd⁡(162,252)=2×3×3=18gcd(162,252)=2×3×3=18. Dividing, 162252=162÷18252÷18=914.252162​=252÷18162÷18​=149​. The clean-jar share is 9/149/14​. Since 9=329=32 and 14=2×714=2×7 share no prime, it is fully reduced.
Practice
A machine stamps fractions equal to 3883​ with bottom ≤80≤80. Allowed bottoms are multiples of 88. How many such fractions fit?
Show the solution
Every fraction equal to 3883​ is 3k8k8k3k​, so its bottom is 8k8k. Needing 8k≤808k≤80 gives k≤10k≤10, so the bottoms run 8,16,24,…,808,16,24,…,80. That is 1010​ fractions. Because 3883​ is already in lowest terms, every equal name has a bottom that is a multiple of 88.
Practice
Prize wheel: 3030 slots labelled n3030n​. Sticker when gcd⁡(n,30)=1gcd(n,30)=1. 30=2×3×530=2×3×5, so nn must miss multiples of 22, 33, 55. How many slots get stickers?
Show the solution
A slot wins when nn misses every prime factor of 30=2×3×530=2×3×5. Cross out the evens, the multiples of 33, and the multiples of 55, and what survives from 11 to 3030 is 1,7,11,13,17,19,23,291,7,11,13,17,19,23,29. That is 88​ slots. With only 3030 numbers in play, listing the survivors is faster than any formula.
